result.text: A guest enters the restaurant when feeling hungry.
He chooses a dish from the changing meal range and waits until it is his turn.
Following this he places his order with the employee.
The employee enters the order into the POS system and collects the money from the guest.
After the payment, the employee sets up a buzzer and passes it on to the guest with the following information: "When the buzzer rings, your dinner is ready".
Afterwards the employee informs the chef of the new meal order.
The chef prepares the meal and places it in the service hatch.
He then informs the employee that he has placed the finished meal in the service hatch.
As soon as the employee is aware that the meal is ready he sets off the guest's buzzer.
This is how the guest finds out that his meal is ready for collection.
He can pick up his meal and eat it.
As soon as the guest appears at the service hatch, the employee hands over his meal.
Should a guest not react to the buzzer, the employee calls for him after 5 minutes, if necessary several times in a row.

When the description names an activity or milestone for which a BPMN task is being labeled: Label the task to preserve the action and purpose stated in the description; do not substitute a related but different action or milestone.

When the description establishes an overarching subject or context that applies to several separately stated activities: Label each task with its stated action and purpose, omitting repeated context and qualifiers unless needed to distinguish the activity; do not add unsupported details.

result.text: A guest enters the restaurant when feeling hungry.
He chooses a dish from the changing meal range and waits until it is his turn.
Following this he places his order with the employee.
The employee enters the order into the POS system and collects the money from the guest.
After the payment, the employee sets up a buzzer and passes it on to the guest with the following information: "When the buzzer rings, your dinner is ready".
Afterwards the employee informs the chef of the new meal order.
The chef prepares the meal and places it in the service hatch.
He then informs the employee that he has placed the finished meal in the service hatch.
As soon as the employee is aware that the meal is ready he sets off the guest's buzzer.
This is how the guest finds out that his meal is ready for collection.
He can pick up his meal and eat it.
As soon as the guest appears at the service hatch, the employee hands over his meal.
Should a guest not react to the buzzer, the employee calls for him after 5 minutes, if necessary several times in a row.

result.process_description:
A guest enters the restaurant when feeling hungry. 
He chooses a dish from the changing meal range and waits until it is his turn. 
Following this he places his order with the employee. The employee enters the order into the POS system and collects the money from the guest. 
After the payment, the employee sets up a buzzer and passes it on to the guest with the following information: 
"When the buzzer rings, your dinner is ready". 
Afterwards the employee informs the chef of the new meal order. 
The chef prepares the meal and places it in the service hatch. 
He then informs the employee that he has placed the finished meal in the service hatch. 
As soon as the employee is aware that the meal is ready he sets off the guest's buzzer. 
This is how the guest finds out that his meal is ready for collection. 
He can pick up his meal and eat it. 
As soon as the guest appears at the service hatch, the employee hands over his meal. 
Should a guest not react to the buzzer, the employee calls for him after 5 minutes, if necessary several times in a row.

args.text: When a process description describes work or communication involving distinct participants, model each participant in the appropriate pool and represent communication between pools with message flows in the direction the information or item is sent.

trace.reason: Check documented collaboration guidelines for overlap or conflict before proposing a general rule.

result.rule: Create bpmn:collaboration when distinct participants interact and represent every participant as a bpmn:participant pool.
Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.
Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.
Direct each message flow from sender to receiver. Its endpoints must belong to different pools and be valid interaction nodes.
Use sequence flows inside one participant process and message flows between different participants. Never use sequence flow across pools.
Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.

args.text: When a process description describes communication between distinct participants, model each participant as a pool and represent each described communication with a message flow from the sender to the receiver, using appropriate interaction nodes.

result.rule: When the description distinguishes a user-facing software interface from a backend process and states that users receive results or status updates through that interface: Model the interface as a separate participant pool and represent the described communication between it and the backend with message flows.

When the description narrates work performed by a first-person actor and states that the actor communicates with people or organizations outside that work: Model the narrated actor as a participant pool in the collaboration, with the actor’s described work in its process.

When the description presents one participant's work as following a handoff from another participant: Model the receiving work as connected to that handoff: use sequence flow within the same process, or a message flow to a message-triggered start or catch event in a separate process, rather than an unconnected start-to-end chain.

When the description says an external participant notifies an internal process while continuing its own work: Model the notification as a message flow from the external participant to a receiving message event in the internal process.
